MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In the number 24,613, the digit 4 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Tens
   B. Ones
   C. Thousands
   D. Hundreds

2. Which of these is a factor of 45? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 6
   C. 9
   D. 4

3. What is the 4th multiple of 9? (1 mark)
   A. 13
   B. 36
   C. 27
   D. 45

4. Which of these is a multiple of 8? (1 mark)
   A. 72
   B. 71
   C. 74
   D. 73

5. Which is the largest number: 3,060, 3,006, 3,600, 3,660? (1 mark)
   A. 3,660
   B. 3,006
   C. 3,060
   D. 3,600

6. A trader saved Ksh 4,650 in the first term and Ksh 2,875 in the second term. How much did she save? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 7,515
   B. Ksh 7,525
   C. Ksh 6,425
   D. Ksh 7,625

7. What is the sum when you add 1 to 9,999? (1 mark)
   A. 10,000
   B. 10,001
   C. 99,999
   D. 9,000

8. Which sum checks that 5,432 − 2,718 = 2,714? (1 mark)
   A. 5,432 + 2,714
   B. 2,714 − 2,718
   C. 2,714 + 2,718
   D. 5,432 + 2,718

9. Estimate 9,317 − 4,582 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 4,840
   B. 4,740
   C. 4,750
   D. 4,730

10. What is 25 × 100? (1 mark)
   A. 2,500
   B. 250
   C. 125
   D. 25,000

11. Work out 27 × 13. (1 mark)
   A. 341
   B. 351
   C. 108
   D. 361

12. In 56 ÷ 8 = 7, the number 8 is called the (1 mark)
   A. quotient
   B. remainder
   C. divisor
   D. dividend

13. 38 mangoes are shared equally among 5 children. How many mangoes are left over? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 7
   C. 4
   D. 2

14. What is 45 ÷ 6? (1 mark)
   A. 7 remainder 4
   B. 7 remainder 3
   C. 8 remainder 3
   D. 6 remainder 9

15. What is 85 ÷ 5? (1 mark)
   A. 17
   B. 27
   C. 18
   D. 16

16. Change 25/6 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 4 1/6
   B. 5 1/6
   C. 4 2/6
   D. 1 4/6

17. Which price is the cheapest: Ksh 8.25, Ksh 8.05, Ksh 8.50, Ksh 7.99? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 8.25
   B. Ksh 8.05
   C. Ksh 7.99
   D. Ksh 8.50

18. If n = 6, what is the value of n + 5? (1 mark)
   A. 30
   B. 1
   C. 65
   D. 11

19. If b = 3, what is the value of 2b + 1? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 21
   C. 7
   D. 5

20. In the expression 3m + 2o, what does the letter o stand for if m is a bag of mangoes and 2o is 2 bags of oranges? (1 mark)
   A. One bag of oranges
   B. The number 2
   C. The total number of bags
   D. Two bags of mangoes

21. A fence uses 5 pieces of wire, each 3 m 50 cm long. What is the total length of wire? (1 mark)
   A. 3 m 55 cm
   B. 18 m 50 cm
   C. 17 m 50 cm
   D. 17 m 40 cm

22. A triangle has sides of 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 12 cm
   B. 13 cm
   C. 14 cm
   D. 7 cm

23. A pencil starts at the 4 cm mark on a ruler and ends at the 12 cm mark. How long is the pencil? (1 mark)
   A. 16 cm
   B. 9 cm
   C. 8 cm
   D. 12 cm

24. A pencil starts at the 5 cm mark on a ruler and ends at the 10 cm mark. How long is the pencil? (1 mark)
   A. 6 cm
   B. 10 cm
   C. 5 cm
   D. 15 cm

25. A square is covered with 3 rows of 3 unit squares. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 9 square units
   B. 6 square units
   C. 8 square units
   D. 12 square units

26. Which shape is a cuboid? (1 mark)
   A. A plate
   B. A football
   C. A coin
   D. A matchbox

27. A cuboid is 6 blocks long, 3 blocks wide and 2 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 18 blocks
   B. 36 blocks
   C. 11 blocks
   D. 42 blocks

28. What is 3 3/4 L + 3 1/2 L? (1 mark)
   A. 7 1/4 L
   B. 7 1/2 L
   C. 7 3/4 L
   D. 7 L

29. Which is the best way to read the water level on a measuring jug? (1 mark)
   A. Count the number of handles
   B. Look at the scale level with the water
   C. Look from high above the jug
   D. Look with your eyes closed

30. A goat has a mass of 32 kg and a sheep 27 kg. How much heavier is the goat? (1 mark)
   A. 5 kg
   B. 6 kg
   C. 4 kg
   D. 59 kg

31. How many days are in 3 weeks? (1 mark)
   A. 72 days
   B. 15 days
   C. 21 days
   D. 28 days

32. How can you make Ksh 50 using only 10 shilling coins? (1 mark)
   A. Ten coins
   B. Five coins
   C. Fifty coins
   D. Two coins

33. A tap is usually opened by turning it (1 mark)
   A. down
   B. clockwise
   C. anticlockwise
   D. up

34. If you face north, which direction is on your right? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. West
   C. North
   D. South

35. A half turn makes (1 mark)
   A. a small angle
   B. a right angle
   C. a full turn
   D. a straight line

36. What is the fold line that divides a shape into two matching halves called? (1 mark)
   A. An angle
   B. A vertex
   C. A line of symmetry
   D. A perimeter

37. How many straight sides does a rectangle have? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 3
   C. 4
   D. 5

38. How many lines of symmetry does a triangle with no equal sides have? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 0
   C. 1
   D. 2

39. How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 0
   C. 6
   D. 4

40. Why do we add up the totals in a table? (1 mark)
   A. To change the data
   B. To hide the data
   C. To make the table longer
   D. To check that the numbers are correct

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Divide 47 by 5. Check your answer using multiplication and addition. (3 marks)

42. A farmer had 6,500 seedlings and planted 2,875. How many were left? Estimate first by rounding to the nearest ten. (4 marks)

43. Ksh 3.50 is given as 3 shillings and 50 cents. Write 75 cents and 5 cents as decimals of a shilling. (3 marks)

44. Divide 84 by 4 and check your answer. (3 marks)

45. A learner says that a half turn is the same as two quarter turns. Is the learner right? Explain. (2 marks)

46. A class has 30 pupils. Two fifths of them walk to school. How many pupils walk to school? (3 marks)

47. Draw an angle using a ruler. Name the vertex and the arms and mark the angle with a small curve. (3 marks)

48. Amina says the perimeter of a rectangle 8 cm by 5 cm is 13 cm. Explain her mistake and give the correct perimeter. (3 marks)

49. A tank has 50 L of water. The family uses 18 L. How much water is left? (2 marks)

50. 38 mangoes are shared equally among 5 children. How many does each child get and how many are left over? (3 marks)

51. Write the next three numbers in the pattern 5, 9, 13, 17, ... and state the rule. (3 marks)

52. A bus leaves at 10:30 a.m. and arrives at 2:15 p.m. How long is the journey? (3 marks)

53. A gate opens through a half turn from its closed position. Describe the angle between the gate and the wall in its closed position. (2 marks)

54. Add 6,478 and 2,355 and check by estimating to the nearest ten. (4 marks)

55. A farmer joins 4 pieces of wire, each measuring 2 m 30 cm, to make one long wire. Find the length of the long wire. (3 marks)

56. A film begins at 4:20 p.m. and runs for 1 hour 40 minutes. Find the time at which it ends. (2 marks)

57. Describe a pattern of shapes that you can make with squares and triangles, and write down the first six shapes. (3 marks)

58. Change 3 hours to minutes and 2 days to hours. (2 marks)

59. Wanjiru buys goods worth Ksh 750 and pays with a Ksh 1,000 note. How much change should she get? Check your answer. (3 marks)

60. Wangari buys 24 exercise books at Ksh 18 each. Estimate the total cost by rounding to the nearest ten, then work out the exact cost. (4 marks)

61. Describe the difference between a clockwise and an anticlockwise turn. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #16 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Thousands
   Counting from the right the places are ones, tens, hundreds, thousands and ten thousands. The digit 4 is in the thousands place.

2. C — 9
   45 ÷ 9 = 5 with nothing left over, so 9 is a factor of 45. The others leave a remainder.

3. B — 36
   Multiply 9 × 4 = 36. It is the 4th multiple of 9.

4. A — 72
   72 = 8 × 9, so 72 is a multiple of 8.

5. A — 3,660
   Compare the digits from the left. The largest number is 3,660.

6. B — Ksh 7,525
   Add 4,650 + 2,875 = 7,525 Ksh.

7. A — 10,000
   9,999 + 1 = 10,000. Each 9 turns into 0 and a 1 is carried to a new place.

8. C — 2,714 + 2,718
   Addition undoes subtraction. 2,714 + 2,718 = 5,432, the starting number.

9. B — 4,740
   9,317 rounds to 9,320 and 4,582 rounds to 4,580. 9,320 − 4,580 = 4,740.

10. A — 2,500
   Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 25 × 100 = 2,500.

11. B — 351
   27 × 3 = 81 and 27 × 10 = 270. 81 + 270 = 351.

12. C — divisor
   The number we divide by is the divisor. 56 is the dividend and 7 is the quotient.

13. A — 3
   38 ÷ 5 = 7 remainder 3. Each child gets 7 and 3 are left.

14. B — 7 remainder 3
   6 × 7 = 42 and 45 − 42 = 3. So 45 ÷ 6 = 7 remainder 3. Check: 7 × 6 + 3 = 45.

15. A — 17
   5 × 17 = 85, so 85 ÷ 5 = 17.

16. A — 4 1/6
   25 ÷ 6 = 4 remainder 1. The whole number is 4 and the fraction is 1/6, so 25/6 = 4 1/6.

17. C — Ksh 7.99
   Compare the shillings first. 7 is less than 8, so Ksh 7.99 is the smallest.

18. D — 11
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 11.

19. C — 7
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 7.

20. A — One bag of oranges
   The letter o stands for one bag of oranges. The number 2 in front tells us how many bags.

21. C — 17 m 50 cm
   350 × 5 = 1750 cm = 17 m 50 cm.

22. A — 12 cm
   Add all three sides: 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 cm.

23. C — 8 cm
   Subtract the start from the end: 12 − 4 = 8 cm.

24. C — 5 cm
   Subtract the start from the end: 10 − 5 = 5 cm.

25. A — 9 square units
   Area = 3 × 3 = 9 square units.

26. D — A matchbox
   A matchbox has six rectangular faces, so it is a cuboid.

27. B — 36 blocks
   One layer has 6 × 3 = 18 blocks. There are 2 layers, so the volume is 18 × 2 = 36 blocks.

28. A — 7 1/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 3 3/4 L + 3 1/2 L = 7 1/4 L.

29. B — Look at the scale level with the water
   Reading level with the water gives the correct mark.

30. A — 5 kg
   32 − 27 = 5 kg.

31. C — 21 days
   1 week = 7 days, so 3 × 7 = 21 days.

32. B — Five coins
   5 × 10 = 50, so five 10 shilling coins make Ksh 50.

33. C — anticlockwise
   Most taps open when turned anticlockwise and close when turned clockwise.

34. A — East
   Facing north, east is on your right, west on your left and south behind you.

35. D — a straight line
   A half turn is two right angles, which form a straight line.

36. C — A line of symmetry
   If the two halves match exactly, the fold is a line of symmetry.

37. C — 4
   A rectangle has four straight sides.

38. B — 0
   No fold makes the two halves match.

39. A — 2
   It folds along the line joining the middles of the long sides and the line joining the middles of the short sides.

40. D — To check that the numbers are correct
   If the total does not match the number of items counted, we must count again.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: 9 remainder 2. Check: 9 × 5 + 2 = 47.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 9, 1 mark for remainder 2, 1 mark for the check.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate 6,500 − 2,880 = 3,620. Exact: 3,625 seedlings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rounding 2,875 to 2,880 (6,500 stays), 1 mark for the estimate, 1 mark for the exact working, 1 mark for the answer.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: 0.75 and 0.05 of a shilling (Ksh 0.75 and Ksh 0.05)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the idea that 100 cents = 1 shilling, 1 mark for each decimal.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: 21
   Working / marking points: 80 ÷ 4 = 20 (1 mark); 4 ÷ 4 = 1, so 21 (1 mark); check 21 × 4 = 84 (1 mark).

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Yes. A half is made of two quarters, so two quarter turns make one half turn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for yes, 1 mark for the reason.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: 12 pupils
   Working / marking points: 30 ÷ 5 = 6 (1 mark); 6 × 2 = 12 (1 mark); answer with unit (1 mark).

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: A drawing with two straight lines meeting at a point, the point labelled vertex, the lines labelled arms and a curve between them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two straight arms, 1 mark for the vertex, 1 mark for the curve.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: She added only two sides. The perimeter is the distance all the way round, so we add all four sides: 8 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 26 cm.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the mistake, 1 mark for the reason, 1 mark for 26 cm.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: 32 L
   Working / marking points: 50 − 18 = 32. 1 mark for the subtraction and 1 mark for the unit.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Each child gets 7 mangoes and 3 mangoes are left over.
   Working / marking points: 38 ÷ 5 = 7 remainder 3. 1 mark for the division, 1 mark for 7, 1 mark for 3.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rule: add 4. Next numbers: 21, 25, 29.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for the three correct numbers (1 mark if only two are correct).

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 hours 45 minutes
   Working / marking points: 10:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. is 2 h (1 mark); 12:30 to 2:15 p.m. is 1 h 45 min (1 mark); total 3 h 45 min (1 mark).

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: They make a straight line, which is two right angles.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a straight line and 1 mark for two right angles.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: Exact 8,833. Estimate 6,480 + 2,360 = 8,840, which is close.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the exact sum with regrouping, 1 mark for rounding both numbers, 1 mark for the estimate.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: 9 m 20 cm
   Working / marking points: 230 × 4 = 920 cm (2 marks); 920 cm = 9 m 20 cm (1 mark).

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: 6:00 p.m.
   Working / marking points: 4:20 + 1 h = 5:20 p.m. (1 mark); + 40 min = 6:00 p.m. (1 mark).

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: square, triangle, square, triangle, square, triangle. The pattern repeats a square and a triangle in turn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using both shapes, 1 mark for a clear repeating rule, 1 mark for six correct shapes.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: 180 minutes and 48 hours
   Working / marking points: 3 × 60 = 180 (1 mark); 2 × 24 = 48 (1 mark).

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 250. Check: 750 + 250 = 1,000.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 1,000 − 750, 1 mark for Ksh 250, 1 mark for the check.

60. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate: 20 × 20 = 400. Exact: 24 × 18 = 432 shillings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rounding both numbers, 1 mark for 400, 1 mark for the exact working (24 × 8 = 192 and 24 × 10 = 240), 1 mark for 432.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: A clockwise turn goes the same way as the hands of a clock. An anticlockwise turn goes the opposite way.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct description.
